title: One dead, 14 injured in Bronx apartment explosion: FDNY - NewsBreak
text:
By Spencer Gustafson Henry Rosoff ,
10 hours ago
NORWOOD, The Bronx (PIX11) — One person is dead after an explosion caused a massive fire inside a Bronx apartment building, officials confirmed.
Fire received a report of an explosion at 374 East 209th St. between Decatur Avenue and Parkside Place in Norwood just before 12:30 p.m. on Wednesday, officials said.
Discover more local reporting on our homepage As firefighters battled the flames, the fire was upgraded to a 5-alarm fire just before 2 p.m. Citizen video showed multiple floors of the apartment building engulfed in smoke and flames as operations were ongoing.
Fire officials confirmed that the blaze was on the second and third floors of the five-story building.
Fire Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore confirmed that an explosion did occur, which sparked the fire to break out. Chief of Departments John Esposito said the third floor partially collapsed into the second floor.
Officials said one person was found dead inside the building, two others have life-threatening injuries and two more have serious injuries. Three firefighters have serious injuries as well, according to officials.
A total of 14 people, eight residents and six firefighters, were injured in some capacity.
The Office of Emergency Management posted a notice to residents and commuters to expect smoke and traffic delays in the area as the FDNY attempted to contain the fire.
Discover more local reporting on our homepage One resident was in tears on the street because her animals were trapped inside.
“I take care of service animals that just got out of the hospital. They won’t even let me get them out,” the resident said.
Multiple witnesses described the sound of the reported explosion as bomb-like.
“It sounded like the world was coming to an end,” one woman who lives nearby said. “It sounded like a bomb went off.”
Officials said 18 residents have been displaced as a result of the fire.
